UNITED STATES INDIAN SCHOOL, CARLISLE, PENNSYLVANIA. Name Frank A. Andrews 1. Are you married and if so to whom? No sir 2. What is your present address? Mrs Annie Andrews East 32 St 3. Did you attend or graduate from any other schools after leaving Carlisle? Give names of school and dates if possible I did not attend or graduate any school after leaving Carlisle 4. What is your present occupation? Salary? My present occupation is fireman. My salary $3.50 per day. 5. Do you own your home? No sir I do not. 6. What kind of a house is it? Number of rooms? The house is a larger one with three rooms down stairs and four rooms upstairs 7. How much property do you possess? Stock No stock Land Land Real Estate 8. Do you have money in the bank? How much? 9. Have you been in the Indian Service? In what positions? How long in each? Yes, I have been in service. I was a fireman at the school and held it until I left to come home and it was about four months I held it. 10. What other positions have you held since leaving Carlisle? No other position but fireman I have held since I left Carlisle. 11. Have you done anything for the betterment of your people? Write fully address is Tacoma East 32 St Washington 12. Tell me anything else of interest connected with your life. CARLISLE INDIAN PRESS CARLISLE PA Department of the Interior. Mr. M. Friedman Supt. U. S. Indian School Carlisle Pennsylvania Dec 26, 1912 Name: Frank Andrews (married) Tribe: Puyallup Present Address: is Wapato Wash Former Address: "Address from which we heard from you last." Present Occupation: is Farming Remarks: I always think of my sch. days of Carlisle. I will ever be grateful for the training which I received there. Miss Hazard: - Change address and return to N.R.D. 1511 Wapato Wash May 8-12 Supt Friedman: Dear Sir - In reply to your last letter which I received sometime ago, I was indeed glad to hear from you. I am sorry that I couldn't answer sooner because I was so busy at the time I received your letter. I have 60 acres in alfalfa hay and it keep me busy irrigating it every day. I tell you when a man has to depend upon water for living that means he has to do some hard digging. In the spring time the farmers here are very busy making ditches all over these fields so as to carry the water which is needed to irrigate their crop. Another thing we do is that we cut our alfalfa hay three times in one season. My wife and I has a new comes in our family it is the cutest little baby girl and we are both proud of it. I do wish to have the Red Man mailed also to me. They have changed my mail box number now instead of #22 it is now #44. I must close your letter hoping to hear from you. Yours Truly, Frank Andrew Frank Andrews, an ex-student, now living at Wapato, Washington, writes: "It has been a long time since I left the school, but the Arrow is still a great help to me. I feel lost when I don't hear the news from Carlisle. I am well and happy and hope my friends at school are the same. I send my best regards to all of them." NAME AT CARLISLE: Frank Andrews
